senses.gloss: (cmp. סָטָה) [to go astray,] to be demented, foolish. V. שׁוֹטֶה.

units: <cite ref="Tosefta Bava Kamma 4:4">Tosef. B. Kam. IV, 4</cite> <he>שנִישְׁטוּ בעלין</he> ed. Zuck. (Var. <he>שנִשְׁתַּטּוּ</he>) whose owner became insane; <cite ref="Bava Kamma 39b">B. Kam. 39ᵇ</cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Yevamot 14:1">Yeb. XIV, 1</cite> <he>נִשְׁתַּטֵּית וכ׳</he> if the wife becomes insane, he cannot divorce her; <he>נ׳ וכ׳</he> if he becomes insane, he can never divorce her; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be mad; to rage, be impassioned.
units: <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 20">Num. R. s. 20<sup>23</sup></cite> <he>היה נִשְׁטֶה אחריה וכ׳</he> he was mad with passion for her, as we read (<cite ref="Hosea 4:11">Hos. IV, 11</cite>) &c.; Tanḥ. Balak 18 <he>היו משטתה וכ׳</he> (read: <he>היה מִשְׁתַּטֶּה</he>; ed. Bub. 25 <cite ref="U00745"><he>נשטה</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Hosea 4:11">Ib.</cite> <he>והוא נ׳ וכ׳</he> and he in his rage for her slaughtered it to Baal Peor; Num. R. l. c.

<cite ref="Tosefta Niddah 5:17">Tosef. Nidd. V, 17</cite> <he>עד מתי אתם נִשְׁטִין וכ׳</he> how long will you rage? cry to him that created the sea. Tanḥ. Vayera 22 <he>והזקן הוא ה׳ וכ׳</he> and that old man (Abraham) has run mad, and he is going to slay thee.

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 131:1">Yalk. Sam. 131</cite> <he>והיתה צועקת ומִשְׁתַּטָּה … ומִשְׁתַּטֶּה מבחוץ</he> and she screamed and raged within, and David screamed and raged without; <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 34:1">Midr. Till. to Ps. XXXIV</cite> <he>והיו צועקות שתיהן ומַשְׁטוֹת … ומַשְׁטֶה בחוץ</he> and both of them (mother and daughter) screamed and raged &c.

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 846">Yalk. Ps. 846</cite> [read:] <he>מכאן שמשאדם רואה בנים כאילו הוא משתטה</he> from this we learn that, when a man lives to have children, he acts like a fool (in playing with them).
<cite ref="Yevamot 106a">Yeb. 106ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Kamma 116a:4">B. Kam. 116ᵃ</cite> <he>אמר ליה משטה אני בך</he> he may say, I was only jesting with thee.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 175a:9">B. Bath. 175ᵃ</cite> <he>אין אדם משטה בשעת מיתה</he> nobody jests in his dying hour (therefore a dying man’s admission of indebtedness does not require the usual formalities to be binding).
